items.title: MISCOMPILE: two instantiations of one generic function that indexes through a `write()` place share a HOISTED index temporary - the second instantiation emits `const $c = $b;` with `$b` declared only in the first, so it throws `ReferenceError: $b is not defined` at run time
items.kind: miscompile (JS backend; generic instantiation; hoisted temporaries)
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-09 (lane lens-s3's find, A185 S3)
items.discussion: met in std/src/reactive/lens.vl: `fun bump<H>(table: Shared<Table<H>>, id: i32) { table.write().cells[id.as_usize()].users += 1; }` called with two different `H`; the lens binds the index to a local first as the workaround (the comment at the site names this item)
items.body: Repro: the two-line generic above, instantiated twice, run on node. Rec: hoisted temporaries of an indexed `write()` place must be minted per instantiation (or per emitted function), not shared by the generic's declaration; pin as a corpus program that calls the generic with two types and reads the result, plus an inference/transformer unit test on the emitted names. Sizing S-M. A miscompile: rides the next cut.

items.title: A generic helper whose type parameters appear only in its RETURN type (`fun sequence_access<S: Resizable<T>, T>(): Access<S, usize, T>`) passes the checker when called from inside the module that declares the trait, then fails at EMISSION with `internal: a call resolved to Resizable's requirement count, which has no body ... first reached while emitting sequence_access`; the same shape in a user program is refused by the checker (`generic parameter 'S' is missing the bound ': Resizable<T>' required by this call`)
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-09 (lane lens-s3's find, A185 S3; the lab met the checker half on 2026-11-05)
items.discussion: the two halves disagree: the checker admits the call in std's own module and the emitter cannot resolve the trait requirement to a body; outside std the checker refuses with a message that blames a missing bound rather than saying type arguments are not inferred from an expected return type
items.body: Rec: one rule in both places - either infer a call's type arguments from the expected type (then the emitter gets a concrete `S`) or refuse consistently at the checker with a message that says so (`the type arguments of a call are not inferred from its result; write them or pass a value`). Pin both forms. Sizing S.
